title: Multiscale Weyl-support and dyadic chirp product barrier
plain_meaning: A dyadic chirp needs more than the support-count minimum number of pure-shift resolvents.
exact_claim: For N=2^m≥4 and a primitive 2N-th root ζ, C[i,j]=ζ^((i−j)^2) has inverse coefficients q_t=ζ^(−t²)/N. Every literal product of pure-shift resolvents with arbitrary strides and Weyl-monomial gauges representing C needs L≥m+1. Equality L=m in the support count would force unique dyadic subset sums, contradicted by a chirp parallelogram ratio. More generally, Fourier inverse Weyl support is N² for odd N and N²/2 for even N, so products of denominators having q_j Weyl atoms need Πq_j at least that support. The binary reshape of q has rank 2^min(a,m−a).
model: Literal multiplicative Weyl/shift grammar with specified roots; arbitrary diagonal gauges excluded.

title: Two-sided diagonal-gauge Fourier obstruction
plain_meaning: Allowing independent endpoint gauges does not remove the fixed half-grid symmetry obstruction.
exact_claim: For even s≥4, N=s², and the half-y-grid shift Π, a Π-commuting T0 cannot satisfy F=D_out T0 D_in^−1 with arbitrary invertible diagonal endpoints. For unitary endpoint gauges, both operator and relative Frobenius distance are at least g_s=(1/2)sqrt(1−ρ), where ρ=2/[s sin(π/s)]; the limit is about 0.3014051. After k occurrence-wise weight edits the uniform gap is at least (1/2)sqrt(max(0,1−ρ−8k/N)), so exact equality requires k≥ceil(N(1−ρ)/8). Generic gauges give the stronger k≥N/2, but that is not uniform over gauges.
model: Fixed grid involution and legal commuting reference. Exact arbitrary-invertible-gauge impossibility is distinct from the metric result for unitary gauges.

title: Paired Jacobi/CS and denominator-free dual gate
plain_meaning: Complementary blocks couple two rank tests and give stronger conditional unitary gaps.
exact_claim: For the fixed N256 layout, paired complementary blocks of a unitary matrix have equal singular values. When both candidate blocks have rank at most 16 and both baseline squared Frobenius norms are 64, the paired squared Frobenius tail and paired nuclear lower bounds are 96. An explicit cell-energy witness attains 96 in the relaxation of all 64 scalar constraints. The denominator-free dual G=P1 S1 U^−1 S4 P3 supplies necessary bilinear outer-stage rank conditions. Conditional on both outer inverses being exactly unitary, the operator gap exceeds sqrt(2−2sqrt(7)/5), about 0.970412, and the common outer perturbation exceeds 0.485206.

title: Hadamard–Segre and common-eigenvector gauge gate
plain_meaning: Three internal diagonal gauges reduce to a guarded rank-one matrix or common-eigenvector problem.
exact_claim: For fixed invertible A,B,C with every B entry nonzero, put H=FC^−1. The identity F=L A D B E C with invertible diagonal L,D,E holds iff some vector c has all entries nonzero and Z(c)=(A^−1 diag(c)H) divided entrywise by B has rank one with every entry nonzero. When P0 is invertible, T_j=P0^−1 P_j must have a common eigenvector c with c, P0c and the required eigenvalues all nonzero. A nonzero determinant of [T1,T2] rejects every gauge. Eight source-reported four-/six-Green witnesses at N=3,4,6,8 have guarded nonzero determinants modulo 97 and characteristic-zero nonvanishing lifts.
model: Fixed stage data and ordering, three variable diagonal gauges, and all stated nonzero guards. A singular commutator is only a necessary test.
